file.description: a file, as a path read in a root, so anything in the graph can refer to one; its entity id is derived from the path and the root. It carries its contents as `content.body` where the graph keeps them, and goes without where the bytes are kept elsewhere

path.description: the path from the root, `/`-separated and with no leading `/`: as Git spells it in a repository, from the mount on a volume

root.description: what the path is read in: a `repository`, whose files are a path in its tree at any commit and on no disk, or a `volume`, whose files are bytes on a filesystem a machine mounts

lines.description: where in a file this entity sits: lines `start` through `end`. An entry read from a transcript wears the line it was read from; a citation of some lines is a `cites` edge to an entity wearing them, with the text it quoted as `content.body`

end.description: the last line, inclusive; absent when it is the first line alone

volume.description: a filesystem as a machine mounts it, and the root of the files on it; a path on the machine sits on the volume with the longest mount that contains it. Its entity id is derived from the machine and the mount, so the same disk mounted by another machine is another volume

mount.description: the absolute directory the machine mounts it at, such as `/`

occupancy.description: how full a volume was on one UTC day and what filled it, from that day's latest look: the filesystem's bytes, used and free, the bytes a walk of it could read, and the bytes each directory and file on it that takes at least a thousandth of it holds. A later look that day replaces the earlier, so a run of days is how it is trending

free.description: the bytes still free to write; a filesystem may keep more back for its administrator

counted.description: the bytes the walk could read under the mount; the rest of `used` is in directories it could not read, or kept by the filesystem itself

paths.description: the bytes each directory and file taking at least a thousandth of the volume holds, by its path from the mount; a directory's path ends in `/`. A directory listed holds everything listed under it
